Aishwarya Kalpathi | industry = [[Entertainment]] | owner = Kalpathi Family | num_employees = 133 Employees | parent = Kalpathi Investments }} '''AGS Entertainment''' is an Indian film production, distribution company, and [[Multiplex (movie theater)|multiplex]] chain in [[Chennai, Tamil Nadu]]. It was established in 2006 by Kalpathi brothers: S. Aghoram, S. Ganesh, and S. Suresh. AGS has four [[Multiplex (movie theater)|multiplex]] movie theaters across [[Chennai]]. ==History== AGS Entertainment ventured into film production in 2006 with [[Susi Ganesan]]'s ''[[Thiruttu Payale]]'' (2006),{{Cite news|url=http://www.hindu.com/2007/07/17/stories/2007071757720200.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070820012203/http://www.hindu.com/2007/07/17/stories/2007071757720200.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=20 August 2007|title=Yet another 'Jeyam' Ravi-Raja combination|date=17 July 2007|accessdate=13 May 2010|work=[[The Hindu]]|location=Chennai, India}} which was followed by ''[[Santosh Subramaniam]]'' (2008), both emerging commercial successes.{{cite web|url=http://www.top10cinema.com/feature/8877/season-of-ags-entertainments-in-kollywood |title= Season |accessdate=2011-01-28 |url-status=usurped |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110127170719/http://www.top10cinema.com/feature/8877/season-of-ags-entertainments-in-kollywood |archivedate=2011-01-27 }}{{Cite web |last=Shekar |first=Anjana |date=2018-05-07 |title='We saw both sides of Tamil film industry strike': Meet the CEO of AGS Entertainment |url=https://www.thenewsminute.com/features/we-saw-both-sides-tamil-film-industry-strike-meet-ceo-ags-entertainment-80810 |access-date=2023-11-03 |website=The News Minute |language=en}} Their subsequent productions included the [[Masala (film genre)|masala flick]] ''[[Maasilamani]]'' (2009), [[Chimbudevan]]'s [[Western (genre)|Western]] [[comedy film|comedy]] ''[[Irumbukkottai Murattu Singam]]'' (2010), the [[period piece]] ''[[Madrasapattinam]]'', ''[[Bale Pandiya (2010 film)|Bale Pandiya]]'' (2010), [[Myshkin (director)|Myshkin]]'s crime thriller ''[[Yuddham Sei]]'' (2011), [[Bala (director)|Bala]]'s comedy entertainer ''[[Avan Ivan]]'' (2011), [[Prabhu Deva]] directed romance film ''[[Engeyum Kadhal]]'' (2011), ''[[Vellore Maavattam]]'' (2011) starring [[Nandha (actor)|Nandha]], the [[K. V. Anand]]-[[Suriya]] project ''[[Maattrraan]]'' (2012) and [[Atlee (director)|Atlee]] directed sports action film ''[[Bigil]]'' (2019), while the distribution of films includes ''[[Kandhakottai]]'', ''[[Inidhu Inidhu]]'', ''[[Mynaa]]'' and ''[[Payanam (2011 film)|Payanam]]''. In 2013, AGS Entertainment opened their first cinema theatre in [[Villivakkam]], Chennai. Subsequently, in the following year, they launched AGS [[Old Mahabalipuram Road|OMR,Navalur]], and in 2016, another theater in [[T. Nagar|T Nagar]]. extract: AGS Entertainment is an Indian film production, distribution company, and multiplex chain in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. It was established in 2006 by Kalpathi brothers: S. Aghoram, S. Ganesh, and S. Suresh. AGS has four multiplex movie theaters across Chennai.
